linkages: workers to firms via unique person and firm IDs in the spell data
spell data merged with IDA on person and firm IDs for education, wages and firm sector
value added per worker merged onto the labour market history data from the Statistics Denmark accounting survey (used only for validation of the poaching rank)

sample.universe: virtually all individuals residing legally in Denmark aged 15-70 years, weekly labour market histories 1985-2003; analysis restricted to 1994-2003
sample.unit_of_observation: worker-year (annual November matched employer-employee wage panel); employment and unemployment spells for the mobility statistics; firm for the poaching index
selection_rules: truncate individual labour market histories at age 55
discard any labour market history that predates labour market entry as measured by date of graduation from highest completed education
discard all workers ever observed in employment in the public sector, in self-employment, in retirement, or in the agricultural industry
recode non-participation spells as unemployment spells
recode unemployment spells of duration no greater than 13 weeks followed by recall to the same employer as part of the original employment spell
recode unemployment spells of duration 2 weeks or less between two employment spells with different employers as a job-to-job transition within a single employment spell
select the period 1994-2003 for the analysis
trim the annual individual hourly wage at the 1st and 99th percentiles and trend to 2003 levels
poaching index measured only for firms with a total inflow of more than fifteen hires and at least one hire from unemployment (other firms are assigned to the group of firms without a rank)
sample.n_individuals: 782,951 (all years; 1,698,990 job spells, 608,065 unemployment spells, 117,847 firms, 559,920 firm-years)

construction_notes: wage measure: estimate of the average hourly wage for jobs active in the last week of November; no wage information for job spells not overlapping a last week of November
starting wage taken as the wage on record at the first post-transition November cross section date / average wage during the first calendar year of the job
hourly wages trimmed at the 1st and 99th percentiles and trended to 2003 levels

poaching index of firm j: share of all hires made during the 10-year observation window that come directly from other firms; the poaching rank is the firm's position in the cumulative poaching index distribution across firms
individual average unemployment duration denoted tau-bar_0i; unemployment defined broadly (non-participation recoded as unemployment)
firm wage = wage bill per full time worker; firm labour productivity = value added per full time worker (Figure 2 notes)

simulated counterpart: careers of 500,000 workers simulated over 10 years from the estimated model, recording h, p and q; the data selection and observation scheme (including the poaching-rank selection and firm size) are replicated in the simulation
worker and firm heterogeneity distributions discretised to twenty h-values and sixty p-values (hence sixty-one q-values) in estimation
57 auxiliary statistics; r = 0.05, lambda(theta) = 1, labour force = 1, m = 0.091, c_nu0 = 1 fixed; twenty free structural parameters

claims.statement: The CES match production function is estimated to be supermodular: the modularity parameter rho is -7.303, i.e. well below the modular value rho = 1, so worker skill and firm productivity are complements in match output.

treatment.label: Worker skill h and firm productivity p entering the match production function jointly (production complementarity)

definition.value: h in [0,1] is permanent innate worker skill, Beta(beta_0', beta_1') distributed; p in [0,1] is permanent firm productivity, Beta(beta_0, beta_1) distributed; both are unobserved and recovered from the structural model. Their complementarity is governed by rho in f(h,p) = f0[alpha h^rho + (1-alpha) p^rho]^(1/rho): supermodular if rho < 1.

timing.value: permanent types; steady state of the 1994-2003 economy

outcome.label: Match output f(h,p) (CES production function modularity parameter rho)

definition.value: Output of a match between a worker of skill h and a firm of productivity p. The reported estimate is the CES substitution/modularity parameter rho of f(h,p) = f0[alpha h^rho + (1-alpha) p^rho]^(1/rho), estimated by Indirect Inference.

units.value: CES modularity parameter (dimensionless); rho < 1 = supermodular, rho = 1 = modular, rho > 1 = submodular

magnitude.interpretation: "The production function is with an estimate of rho = -7.30 estimated to be supermodular" (p. 174); supermodularity implies positive assortative matching.

estimand.target_population: the Danish private-sector labour market 1994-2003 as represented by the estimated equilibrium model

population.region: Denmark (model estimated on the 1994-2003 Danish analysis panel)

identification.source_of_variation: Firm-rank conditional worker mobility and wage patterns in Danish matched employer-employee data 1994-2003: firms are ranked by the poaching index (the fraction of a firm's hires poached from other firms), and 57 auxiliary statistics on rank-conditional mobility, unemployment durations, re-employment wages and log-wage moments are matched by Indirect Inference.
